smart_pickup.title: UPS Smart Pickup®
smart_pickup.body:
UPS Smart Pickup
®
Save time and the planet by confirming a pickup when you have packages ready for us, eliminating interruptions to your day.
Who Smart Pickups Are For
Dynamic Shippers
Ideal for businesses with regular shipping volume whose needs change day to day.
Time-Savers
Perfect for those who don’t want to schedule a pickup every day.
Economical Senders
Great for customers with varying shipping activity who want to lower their weekly pickup fee.
Enroll in Smart Pickup
Smart Pickup Benefits
Reduce Costs
Save money with a solution designed for shippers who don’t need a daily pickup.
Always-On Package Pickup Flexibility
Eliminate the need for daily scheduling with consistent, reliable access to pickups.
Real-Time Visibility
Gain end-to-end pickup management through live status updates on UPS.com or the UPS Mobile App.
Eco-Friendly
Reduce your carbon footprint by avoiding unnecessary pickups.
Show More
How to Enroll in a UPS Smart Pickup
Step 1: Log In to Your Account
Once in the “Manage Pickups” dashboard, ensure the applicable account is selected. Click on “Pickup Settings”.
Step 2: Select Pickup Options
Under "Pickup Options", select “Automatically when I create a shipment online with UPS Smart Pickup.”
Step 3: Add Pickup Details
Fill out your preferred pickup times and driver instructions, if applicable. Click “Save.”*
Log In to Get Started
*Changes to your pickup settings may take up to 3 business days to be applied.
FAQ
What shipping services are compatible with UPS Smart Pickups?
UPS Smart Pickup service is available on all UPS shipping platforms, including UPS.com Shipping, UPS WorldShip®, UPS CampusShip, and any third-party platform integrated with UPS Pickup and/or transactional Shipping APIs.
UPS Smart Pickup service can also be activated by scanning the account's custom QR code from any smartphone. You can fully manage these settings on the 
UPS Pickup Dashboard
.
UPS Smart Pickup is compatible with all UPS shipping services; however, a Smart Pickup cannot be confirmed by processing a UPS Ground Saver or UPS Worldwide Express Freight shipment. The pickup must be confirmed by processing a package with different service level or by manually confirming the pickup.
What happens if I process my first package after my notify-by time?
Your notify-by time is the latest possible time you will be able to process your first package of the day and receive a same day pickup after confirming your UPS Smart Pickup service. This cutoff is typically one hour before your desired pickup time. You can view it by logging into your profile and viewing your Pickup Options or 
UPS Pickup Dashboard
.
If you process your first package after your notify-by time, your UPS Smart Pickup service will be confirmed for the next business day. You also have the option to schedule a same day, 
one-time pickup
 if needed.
How do I request UPS Smart Pickup service each day?
You must confirm your pickup to schedule UPS Smart Pickup service for that day or the next business day. Once your pickup is scheduled, you’ll receive a Pickup Reference Number (PRN) to reference that pickup.
Using WorldShip:
Set your preferences within WorldShip to automatically schedule UPS Smart Pickup service upon label manifest or prompt the user each day.
Automatically schedule a Smart Pickup:
 Upon processing first shipment of the day, WorldShip will automatically schedule the pickup without additional confirmation by user.
Prompt user prior to scheduling a Smart Pickup:
 Upon processing first shipment of the day, WorldShip will ask the user if they would like to schedule a pickup.
Using UPS.com Shipping:
When creating your shipment, you can choose between the following options in the Shipping Service section to confirm your pickup:
Request today’s Smart Pickup:
 Your pickup will be confirmed for the same day, as long as the first package is processed by the notify-by time.
Request tomorrow’s Smart Pickup:
 Your pickup will be scheduled for the next business day.
Schedule a UPS One-Time Pickup:
 If your notify-by time has already passed, you have the option to schedule a separate pickup from your UPS Smart Pickup service for the same day or next business day.
Using CampusShip:
You will be able to schedule your UPS Smart Pickup service in the Shipment Processing screen and can choose from the following options:
Include this shipment with the Smart Pickup:
 Confirms pickup for the same day if the first package is processed by the notify-by time. Otherwise, a pickup will be scheduled for the next business day.
Schedule a UPS One-Time Pickup:
 A separate pickup from your UPS Smart Pickup service will be scheduled for same day or next business day.
Using a Non-UPS Shipping Platform:
UPS Smart Pickup service customers shipping on third-party platforms integrated with UPS Pickup or transactional Shipping APIs (PLD is transmitted to UPS upon manifest) will automatically confirm their pickup after processing their first shipment of the day.
You may also easily schedule your UPS Smart Pickup service through the 
UPS Pickup Dashboard
. Select Request a Smart Pickup to schedule your pickup or generate your account-specific QR code, which can be printed and scanned from any smartphone to confirm a pickup.
Full UPS Smart Pickup service functionality is also available by integrating the UPS Pickup API, which can be access through the 
UPS Developer Portal
.
How do I access my pickup preferences?
To access and update your pickup preferences:
Log in (if you have not already) and go to your 
UPS Pickup Dashboard
.
Choose your account from the drop-down menu.
Click on “Pickup Settings”, then “Pickup Options”.
View or update pickup type and time options.
How do I find the current status of my UPS Smart Pickup service?
You can view pickup status, details and history by logging into your 
UPS Pickup Dashboard
.

UPS has flexible pickup solutions designed to match the pace of your business.

UPS Saturday Pickup & Delivery
Extend your shipping window with Saturday services, ensuring a driver is available when weekdays just aren’t enough.
Who Saturday Services Are For
Time-Sensitive Shippers
Fit for customers who need weekend pickups or deliveries to keep shipments moving without delay.
Extended Operations
Great for businesses looking to meet customer expectations with faster turnaround times and extended shipping flexibility.
Weekend Focused

FAQ
Does UPS pick up and deliver on weekends, including Saturday and Sunday?
UPS offers Monday through Saturday services for residential and commercial packages. However, there are no pickups nor deliveries on Sunday.
What time does UPS pick up packages?
For Saturday Pickup, UPS will collect your package(s) within the selected window upon scheduling your recurring or One-Time Pickup.
Are there additional fees for Saturday deliveries or pickups?
Saturday Delivery:
For ground residential delivery packages, there are no additional fees. For Saturday ground commercial delivery packages, there is an additional package fee. There’s no delivery charge if a customer enrolls in commercial delivery services with a scheduled Saturday pickup.
Saturday Pickups must match your Monday through Friday pickup type, except if it’s a One-Time Pickup.
Learn the latest pricing for UPS One-Time Pickup by searching for “Value-Added Services – Weekend Services” in the 
UPS Rates & Service Guide

In many areas, UPS will simply leave the shipment on your doorstep. You always have the option of registering for

What is a UPS Access Point?
UPS Access Point locations are convenient pickup and drop-off points located at participating retailers and The UPS Store locations. They provide a secure, flexible way to receive, ship or return eligible packages without waiting at home for a delivery.
How long do UPS Access Point locations hold packages?
You have seven calendar days to pick up your package from a UPS Access Point.
What do I need to pick up my package from a UPS Access Point?
Normally you’ll need your ID and tracking number. Special circumstances may call for additional information such as a Package Release Code or utility bill.
Can I change to a pickup location anytime?
UPS My Choice has excellent flexibility to have your pickup location updated. It will show you all available options that can be chosen at that specific time.
Can I print labels, get packaging materials and other shipping help at a UPS Access Point?
You can print at locations that provide Mobile Barcode service if you have a barcode to print a label purchased at UPS.com or provided by a shipper. If you are looking to purchase a label at the location, get packaging materials or other shipping help, look at either The UPS Store, Staples, Authorized Shipping Outlet or Authorized Service Provider locations.

Manage Billing and Invoices
Whether you need to pay a shipping bill or manage multiple invoices, we have convenient and secure tools that make it easy.
Updates to the CSV Header Row File
As of September 2026, the CSV header row file's column length will be increasing the total number of columns from 250 to 270.

Payments, Invoices, & Receipts
How can I pay my UPS invoice?
We recommend making payments using one of our convenient online payment tools:
You can make a one-time payment of a UPS invoice using our 
Pay Now
 feature. No enrollment or login is required; just enter the information from the invoice you want to pay, then provide a payment method.
Or, if you receive regular invoices for your UPS package (6-digit) or UPS Supply Chain Solutions® (9-digit) account, you may prefer to 
enroll in the UPS Billing Center
. You’ll need a copy of a recent invoice for each account you wish to enroll.
How can I pay UPS by sending an ACH credit?
The fastest way to have your payment credited to your account is to pay using the 
UPS Billing Center
 (it’s easy to enroll using information from your UPS invoice) or our 
Pay Now
 app (no enrollment or login needed).
If you prefer to send an ACH credit payment directly from your own bank or other ACH payment provider, the 
UPS Payment Guide
 has instructions for setting up your payment.
Be sure you understand your ACH payment provider’s fee structure and settlement schedule. Some institutions may not credit UPS’ account for up to four banking days and may charge higher fees for faster payments. Keep in mind that payments made using the 
UPS Billing Center
 or 
Pay Now
 apps do not have any additional fees when you choose ACH and payment is typically reflected on your UPS account within 24 hours.
If making ACH payments outside of the UPS Billing Center or Pay Now apps, contact your ACH payment provider to set up payments using the CTX 820 format. This format can help avoid processing delays because it includes remittance details with your payment (the invoices you are paying and the amount to apply to each). If you cannot send your ACH via the CTX 820 format, you must manually send the remittance information via a spreadsheet (invoice numbers and invoice amounts) to paymentremit@ups.com.
How can I pay COD charges or import charges (duties & taxes) so that UPS can deliver my package?
When COD charges or import charges need to be paid prior to delivery, the 
tracking page on UPS.com
 will display a "
Pay Now
" link enabling you to make payment.
If you are not expecting a COD or import package, be extra cautious of any message saying that funds are required for package delivery. Only a few packages require money for delivery: Collect on Delivery (COD) packages and import packages with duties or taxes due. 
Tracking your package
 is the safest way to verify if any fees are due. Visit our 
Protect Yourself from Fraud and Scams
 page to learn best practices to help avoid fraud.
I paid for my shipment when I printed my label on UPS.com. How do I get a receipt?
If you have a UPS.com username and you were logged in when you created your shipping label, then your shipment was saved in your 
Shipping History
. Simply locate the shipment in your list, and use the menu to retrieve your receipt.
How can I have my payment terms extended so I don't keep getting late fees?
The easiest way to avoid late payment fees is to 
enroll in the UPS Billing Center
 so you receive your invoices electronically, avoiding days in transit for postal delivery. Paying your invoice electronically (either in the Billing Center or with our 
Pay Now
 feature) will also eliminate days required to deliver and manually process your check.
If you still feel you need to have your payment terms adjusted, contact the UPS sales executive responsible for your account. If you do not have a sales executive assigned, you may contact the billing support phone number printed on your invoice.
How can I get a copy of my invoice?
If you are signed up for the 
UPS Billing Center
, your invoices are available there for 56 weeks after the date it was issued.
If you need a duplicate copy of an invoice and are not signed up for the Billing Center, reach out to the billing support team at 
1-800-811-1648
 (for domestic & export invoices) or 
1-866-493-7140
 (for import invoices).

What is the IEEPA tariff refund process?
The U.S. Court of International Trade has required U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to refund the 2025 tariffs collected under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) that were invalidated by the Supreme Court.
Effective April 20, 2026, CBP will launch the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) platform for Importers of Record (IORs) to begin submitting IEEPA tariff refund requests.
Read 
here

Why am I being charged duties and taxes and what's the difference?
When you order something from another country, you may see extra charges on your shipment. These fees are not added by the seller or the shipping company, they are required by the government. Here’s a breakdown of the common charges and how they differ:
A customs duty (AKA tariff)
 is a charge imposed by a government on goods imported into a country. These charges help regulate international trade and protect domestic industries. The amount is typically based on several factors, including the product’s harmonized tariff code, country of origin, and declared value.
Tax
, on the other hand, is an additional cost applied to products, based on a standard percentage set by the government to fund public expenditures. Common taxes of this kind include Sales Tax and Value-Added Tax.
Sales tax is a domestic tax applied to goods and services sold within a country. It’s charged at the point of sale and collected by local or state governments.
Value-Added Tax (VAT) is a consumption tax levied on the value added to goods and services at each stage of production and distribution.
Other types of taxes may apply depending on the country, such as Excise Tax, which targets specific goods like fuel or alcohol.
For more information on import fees click 
here
.
Who pays the tariffs?
The responsible party for payment of tariffs imposed on foreign goods is based on the Incoterms
®
 - or “International Commerce Terms” of the shipment. Incoterms
®
 are a uniform set of international trade standards that outline who is responsible for transportation, cargo insurance, export and import formalities, payment of duties and taxes, and at what point risk transfers from the seller to the buyer.
How will the new tariffs impact me?
US trade policy changes will likely increase landed costs due to tariffs and require adjustments to import declarations. Businesses may need to adjust pricing or explore alternative supply chains to manage costs effectively.
How can I stay compliant with new regulations?
Provide complete and accurate commercial invoice information including:
Product details and description of goods
Country-of-origin/manufacture of the goods
10-digit Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS)
Quantity and value of items in the shipment
For shipments requiring formal entry, an Importer Tax ID with Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Social Security Number (SSN) is required
Include the recipient’s email and contact information to ensure UPS can contact the recipient for collection of duty and taxes or additional forms if necessary.
Please click 
here
 to learn more.
How do I know what my item’s HTS/HS Code is?
An HS (Harmonized System) or HTS code is a number used worldwide to classify the item you’re shipping. Customs agencies use this code to determine duties, taxes, and whether your item can enter the destination country.
To find the correct code, start with a clear, precise description of your item. The first 6 digits are standardized globally (HS code), while additional digits (HTS) vary by country for more specific classification.

In most cases, yes. All reciprocal tariffs are stacked on top of existing Most Favored Nation duties, except for the European Union. However, reciprocal tariffs do not stack with Section 232 tariffs, and some products may qualify for exclusions.

How To Pack & Ship a Package
New to shipping or need a refresher? Read on for easy steps to ship with UPS.
Ship Now

1. Get Your Package Ready for Shipping
Follow these steps for a successful shipment.
Protect Your Items With Packaging Materials
Carefully wrap items separately and use cushioning material to protect your precious cargo.
Securely Seal Your Shipping Box
Remove any old labels or shipping markings. Then, seal your box with plastic or nylon tape at least two inches wide.
Follow UPS Packaging Guidelines
For additional support and confidence in your packing, review our packaging tips.
Order Supplies
View Packaging Tips
2. Measure and Weigh Your Package
Not all packages are made the same. Let us help you get the right dimensions.
Measure the length, width and height. The longest side of the package will be the length.
Round up to the nearest whole number when taking your measurements. For example, 1 to 1.49 will be considered 1, while 1.5 to 1.99 will be considered 2.
To calculate the weight, weigh yourself holding the package, then weigh yourself alone. Subtract one from the other to get the package weight, or utilize our 
flat rate shipping
 options.
Keep these measurements handy. You’ll need them to create your shipment.
Want to skip this step? Use our 
flat rate shipping

Show More

What size and weight limits are there for packages?
Packages can be up to 150 lbs and up to 108 inches long

guidelines

freight shipping services

To accurately determine length and girth, use the formula: Length + 2x Width + 2x Height

How do I ship a passport or important documents?
If you're using your own packaging to ship a valuable, thin item – such as a passport or personal record – we recommend using a small box for the best protection. If you need help finding the right size, stop by 
The UPS Store
 and we'll help you find the perfect fit. You can also order the UPS Mini Express Box or UPS Express

here

How do I use my electronic scale for online shipments?
Already have a UPS-approved scale? Awesome! You can connect your scale to your laptop or desktop computer to help speed things up. First, update your shipping preferences to activate the scale. 
Sign in using the link here
 and mark the checkbox Weigh My Packages With My USB-Connected Scale, then click Save.
Note: UPS CampusShip users will need to update their preferences on 
the CampusShip site
. After logging in, select Shipping Preferences on the left-hand side and click on View/Edit to expand your Shipping Options. Mark the checkbox for Use My USB Scale and finish by clicking Update.
Once you’ve set your preferences to allow for your scale, return to the Create a Shipment page and authorize the installation of a downloaded component. After completion, the package weight will show up in the weight field. The Weigh It button will then capture the current scale reading.

What shipping labels are required for Domestic Air?
Your domestic shipments using air services require that you use a label printed from an automated shipping system (like UPS.com) or a UPS Air Shipping Document. The ASD combines your address label, tracking label and shipping record into one form. Specific ASDs are available for:
